1|# Wave 28b re-acceptance (handoffs 40-44) - decisions for wave 28c
2|
3|Panel 8937563b on e5c6992 (range 1de388e..e5c6992), routed, required glm-5.3 and mimo-v2.6-pro: glm ACCEPT
4|(F41-1 minor), muse-spark ACCEPT (F44-1..2 minor, F44-3..6 note), mimo HOLD after a timeout continuation
5|(F42-1..6 major, F42-7..9 minor), qwen3.8-max HOLD after a timeout continuation (F43-1 major, F43-2..3 minor,
6|F43-4..7 note). All four confirm the eighteen findings of the previous round implemented; F35-1, F36-2..11 and
7|F37-1..6 are verified; F36-1 (operator text in telemetry) is narrowed into F42-1 (the model pattern). Two HOLDs,
8|one of them from a required reviewer: wave 28c fixes every finding below.
9|
10|## Telemetry
11|
12|D1. The model name is a CLOSED list (F42-1 major, F43-2): the bridge ships a list of published model names per
13|    vendor class (the models the README documents and the ones its rosters have run); `details.model` and the
14|    tag carry a name only when it EQUALS a list entry after lower-casing; anything else is `other`. No pattern,
15|    no version wildcard. A new model reads `other` until a release adds it; the README says so.
16|D2. `-Forget` never strands data (F42-2 major, F43-1 major, F44-4): with `-PublicRef`, the local deletion runs
17|    ONLY after the intake confirmed the DELETE (2xx); any other answer leaves the salt, the spool and the
18|    counters untouched, prints why, exits non-zero, and can be repeated with the right reference. `-Forget
19|    -Local` alone deletes locally and says in one line that the intake still holds what was sent, and how to
20|    remove it (`-Forget -PublicRef <ref>` BEFORE `-Local`, because the instance id dies with the salt) - and
21|    asks for confirmation unless `-Yes`.
22|D3. Local deletion is atomic against producers (F42-3 major): `-Forget` takes the telemetry lock that the
23|    spool append and the salt creation also take; while it holds it, it writes a `forgetting` marker; a
24|    producer that meets the lock or the marker drops its event (counted) instead of recreating the salt or the
25|    spool; the marker is removed last.
26|D4. The flush lock (F42-7, F43-5, F44-2): a lock is taken over ONLY when its owner process is gone (pid and
27|    start time); an old lock with a living owner is left alone and reported (`sender busy since <t>`). Every
28|    sender writes a token into the lock and checks it again immediately before each spool rewrite; a sender
29|    that lost the lock stops without rewriting.
30|D5. The deadline covers the whole flush (F42-8): spool enumeration, reads and rewrites count against the 60 s;
31|    the sender checks the clock before every local step and stops cleanly when it has passed.
32|D6. The sender's environment (F41-1, F42-9): the allow list gains the proxy variables in both cases
33|    (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`) and the trust inputs (`SSL_CERT_FILE`,
34|    `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`); the README lists the whole
35|    allow list.
36|D7. The spool append does not hold the task write lock (F43-4): inside the lock the event is built and
37|    appended with a wait of at most 1 s; when that fails the run retries for up to 5 s after the lock is
38|    released, and only then warns (console, the detached status record) and counts the event as not spooled.
39|
40|## Process tree and health
41|
42|D8. No pid-only identity (F42-4 major): a descendant whose start time cannot be read is neither killed by pid
43|    nor counted as gone - the kill is `not confirmed: start time of pid <n> unreadable` and the bridge leaves
44|    that process alone.
45|D9. `pgrep` errors are errors (F42-5 major): exit 1 (no match) is an empty child set; any other non-zero exit,
46|    or a timeout, is a failed enumeration and goes to the next method (`ps`, `/proc`); when all fail, the kill
47|    is unconfirmed.
48|D10. The health journal loses nothing silently (F42-6 major, F44-1): an unparsable line is moved to
49|     `<journal>.bad` (appended, with the time), counted in the warning `health journal: <n> unreadable
50|     line(s) kept in <file>`, and the journal is truncated only by the number of bytes that were applied or
51|     moved - never blindly to zero.
52|
53|## Member control and documentation
54|
55|D11. A reviewer that compacts is seen (F43-3, F44-6): when the engine reports a compaction in its stream, the
56|     ledger records `compactions: <n>` and the run warns `the reviewer compacted its context <n> time(s) - the
57|     reply may rest on a summary of the brief`; the prompt of a member that has `context_tokens` ends with one
58|     line that names the brief file again ("before you answer, re-read the brief: <path>"). Which event the
59|     installed codex emits on compaction is looked up first; if none is observable, the ledger says
60|     `compactions: unknown` for such members and the README says so.
61|D12. The test-mode line also appears in the dry run (F44-5); the README states where it appears and where it
62|     does not (a refused run).
63|D13. The CHANGELOG states the runs as they were (F43-7), and wave 28c ends with one clean full suite on EACH
64|     host for the final code.
65|D14. The idle watchdog rule, revision 6 (the operator's decision of 2026-09-30): until a host lets the agent
66|     compact itself there are two states - while work runs or is awaited the context is kept warm always; when
67|     idle the agent writes the handover at idle wake 2, removes the wake and tells the operator the cheap ways
68|     back. The branch "keep the wake for half the refreshes a cold resume is worth" is removed from the skill
69|     and the README; the boundary tables stay as the operator's guide for a manual compaction; README names
70|     the launch option that bounds the context (`--autocompact <tokens>` on the host it was checked on).
71|Accepted as limitations, documented in one sentence each: F44-3 and F43-6 (the vendor class is derived from the
72|host name; a private gateway under a vendor's domain reads as that vendor).
73|

1341|    those names in every turn's event stream; the ledger's `compactions` is n (with the warning `the
1342|    reviewer compacted its context <n> time(s) - the reply may rest on a summary of the brief`),
1343|    `unknown` for a member with `context_tokens` when none was reported - with the installed codex

1345|    brief ends with ``Before you answer, re-read the brief: `<path>`.`` - the last line before the

1348|    preview's `warnings[]` held it); now checked (`harness-host` TESTLINE) and documented: the line
1349|    appears on a committed run, a dry run, a panel run and a detached run, NOT on a refused run.
1350|  - D13 (F43-7) The wave 28b counts above state the runs as they were; wave 28c ends with one clean
1351|    full suite on EACH host for its final code (below).
1352|  - D14 The waiting rule, revision 6 (the operator's decision of 2026-09-30): until a host lets the
1353|    agent compact itself there are two states - while work runs or is awaited the context is kept
1354|    warm always; when idle the handover at idle wake 2, the wake removed, one line to the operator
1355|    with the cheap ways back. The "keep the wake for half the refreshes a cold resume is worth
1356|    (40 / 20 / 10)" branch is removed from the coordinate skill and the README (and from
1357|    `harness-host`'s recomputation; the boundary tables and their recomputation stay); the README
1358|    and the skill name the launch option `--autocompact <tokens>` (Claude Code 2.1.285 `--help`,

1379|### Known limitations
1380|
1381|- (wave 28c) The telemetry vendor class is derived from the endpoint's host NAME only (F43-6,
1382|  F44-3): a private gateway, relay or proxy under a vendor's domain reads as that vendor. A reviewer's
1383|  compaction is seen only when its engine reports it in the event stream: the installed codex-cli
1384|  0.155.1's `exec --json` reports none, so a member with `context_tokens` records `compactions`
1385|  `unknown` (F43-3, F44-6).
1386|
1387|- (wave 26b; wave 26c) The stall cut reads the growth of the event stream and the tool calls it
1388|  names, not their meaning: an engine that wrote keep-alive bytes would never stall, a tool call
1389|  whose end event never comes suspends the cut until the timeout; a turn that thinks silently
1390|  for longer than `-StallSec` outside a tool call is stopped (raise the entry's `stall_sec`, or
1391|  `0`).
1392|- (wave 27) The coordinator's host is a hint read from environment markers the host sets and its
1393|  children inherit - a session started inside another host's session may be named by the inner
1394|  one's markers only; the identity (`CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR`) is the coordinator's word, never
1395|  checked. The scrub removes the markers from what the bridge starts; an engine CLI sets its own
1396|  for its own tools. Whether Codex CLI runs the plugin's SessionStart hook (it trusts a plugin's
1397|  hooks first) and substitutes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in the skills is checked by the live D9 run,
1398|  not by a harness (the fallbacks: the AGENTS.md lines, `CODEX_CONSULT_ROOT`, `-Explain`).
1399|  (wave 27b) The scrub list is exact names from what the hosts set on 2026-09-29: a variable a
1400|  later host version adds is inherited until it is listed. A host that sets no marker (Kimi Code)
1401|  is `unknown`; a claude-code session started inside a Z Code session is named `zcode`. The Z Code
1402|  install and the Kimi Code skills directory are verified; their live coordinator runs are pending.
1403|- (wave 26b) The machine-wide health file is per user profile (`<codex home>`): runs under another
1404|  account or `CODEX_HOME` do not see each other; a `running[]` row of a bridge killed hard stays
1405|  until the next write prunes it (its pid is then gone); two panels that check the count at the
1406|  same instant can both start a member (no reservation - the count is advisory).
1407|- (wave 26b; wave 26c) `-Kick` reaches a member only while one of its engine turns runs or right
1408|  after it exited (it polls there); between turns (the tree check, the commit) a kick waits for the
1409|  next turn or the next run of that number, and `-Kick` exits 3 after 10 s without an
1410|  acknowledgement.
1411|- (wave 26) A panel's size bounds the members STARTED; a member that fails, is refused at launch
1412|  (its peak window, a limit hit meanwhile) or is killed is not replaced (no backfill).
1413|- (wave 26) The routing score depends on the marks recorded with `-Rate`: an unrated consultation
1414|  counts nothing, and marks are missing-not-at-random (a structured reviewer is easier to rate).
1415|  Reproducibility of a draw holds for the same eligible set and scores - a new mark changes the
1416|  weights, so the same seed may seat differently later (the ledger's `panel.routing` records what
1417|  was used).
1418|- (wave 26) `-Require` on a single run is a gate only (the run is still the `-Provider`'s); a
1419|  roster walk (no `-Provider`) refuses `-Require`.
1420|- (wave 26) `panel.started`/`panel.usable` are written by the panel run after the last member; a
1421|  panel run that dies first leaves them `null`.
1422|- A continuation only follows the MAIN turn's kill; a killed denial retry or format repair is
1423|  salvaged and names the resume command, but gets no continuation of its own.
1424|- No continuation when the thread of the killed turn is unknown (a codex stream without
1425|  `thread.started` whose rollout does not name the consultation id).
1426|- The salvage reads what the event stream holds: codex emits a reasoning or message item only
1427|  when it completes, so text of an item in flight at the kill is not in it.
1428|- The listing, `-Short` and the hook read the ledgers of the repository they run in (now
1429|  said on the `endpoint health:` line); a limit recorded in another repository stays invisible
1430|  there until a run in this one hits it.
1431|- (wave 24c) The tree check compares file contents: a file-mode change (chmod) or a change that
1432|  is only staged during a run is not a tree change (`tree_sha256`, the review binding, still
1433|  moves with both).
1434|- (wave 24c) Whether a 429 is a burst is read from its text: a real quota whose 429 names nothing
1435|  but the status is out for 10 minutes only - the next run after that hits it again and records
1436|  it again.
1437|- (wave 25) `-Detach` does not probe the task lock or re-run the time-dependent health/peak
1438|  selection in the foreground: a consultation that takes the task in between makes the
1439|  background refuse (its status: `done`, exit 1, the refusal line) - the foreground's exit 0
1440|  means "started", not "usable".
1441|- (wave 25) The macOS/Linux background (`/bin/sh -c 'exec nohup ...'`) is not exercised by the
1442|  Windows-only harnesses.
1443|- (wave 25) Killing only a detached panel's background process (not its tree) leaves its members
1444|  running to their end; `-Status` says `died` meanwhile and the task stays refused until their
1445|  records clear, as after any killed panel run.
1446|- (wave 25) A single run's summary in the status file stops at `events file:`; the reply itself
1447|  is in the reply file and the log. `-Status` prints non-ASCII text through the console's code
1448|  page, as every bridge output does; the status file and the log are UTF-8.

9347|# 'unknown' when it cannot be read.
9348|function Get-BridgeVersion {
9349|    if ($null -ne $script:BridgeVersion) { return $script:BridgeVersion }
9350|    $v = 'unknown'
9351|    try {
9352|        $mf = Join-Path (Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot) '.claude-plugin') 'plugin.json'
9353|        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $mf -PathType Leaf) {
9354|            $c = [string](Get-PropertyValue (ConvertFrom-Json -InputObject (Read-SharedText -Path $mf)) 'version' '')
9355|            if ($c -match '^[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z.+-]{0,31}$') { $v = $c }

9362|# Where telemetry keeps its files, under the Codex home; $null without one. { Home; Spool (the
9363|# directory); Salt; Last (the last flush's result); Lock (the sender's lock); Notice (the marker of
9364|# the notice for this plugin version); NotSpooled (wave 28b, D6: the events not spooled since the
9365|# last flush, one NDJSON line each); (wave 28c, D3) TelLock (THE telemetry lock of the producers, the
9366|# salt's creation and -Forget) and Forgetting (the marker -Forget writes while it deletes) }.
9367|function Get-TelemetryPaths {
9368|    $h = Get-CodexHome
9369|    if (-not $h) { return $null }
9370|    $spool = Join-Path $h 'telemetry-spool'
9371|    return [pscustomobject]@{
9372|        Home       = $h
9373|        Spool      = $spool
9374|        Salt       = (Join-Path $h 'telemetry-salt')
9375|        Last       = (Join-Path $spool '.last')
9376|        Lock       = (Join-Path $spool '.flush.lock')
9377|        Notice     = (Join-Path $h ('telemetry-notice-' + (Get-BridgeVersion)))
9378|        NotSpooled = (Join-Path $h 'telemetry-not-spooled.ndjson')
9379|        TelLock    = (Join-Path $h 'telemetry.lock')
9380|        Forgetting = (Join-Path $h 'telemetry-forgetting')
9381|    }
9382|}
9383|
9384|# (wave 28c, D3 / F42-3) THE telemetry lock <codex home>/telemetry.lock - taken by every spool append
9385|# of a producer (Add-TelemetryEvent, a complaint kept), by the salt's creation and by -Forget -Local:
9386|# an OPEN HANDLE (FileShare.None), so the OS releases it when its holder dies (it is never stale; the
9387|# empty file stays). While -Forget holds it, the marker <codex home>/telemetry-forgetting says so and
9388|# is removed LAST; a producer that meets the marker (or a lock that stays busy past its short wait)
9389|# drops its event - counted - instead of recreating the salt or the spool. A marker left by a -Forget
9390|# that died keeps dropping events until -Forget -Local runs again (codex-telemetry.ps1 -Status says
9391|# so). Re-entrant within a process. -IgnoreMarker: -Forget's own entry (it finishes a marker left
9392|# behind), and the not-spooled count. { Ok; Why; Forgetting }.
9393|$script:TelemetryLockStream = $null
9394|$script:TelemetryLockDepth = 0
9395|function Enter-TelemetryLock {
9396|    param([int]$WaitMs = 1000, [switch]$IgnoreMarker)
9397|    $r = [pscustomobject]@{ Ok = $false; Why = ''; Forgetting = $false }
9398|    $p = Get-TelemetryPaths
9399|    if (-not $p) { $r.Why = 'no codex home (CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex)'; return $r }
9400|    $forgettingWhy = "codex-telemetry.ps1 -Forget -Local is deleting the local telemetry data, or did not finish (the marker $($p.Forgetting); run -Forget -Local again to finish it)"
9401|    if ($script:TelemetryLockStream) {
9402|        if (-not $IgnoreMarker -and [IO.File]::Exists($p.Forgetting)) { $r.Forgetting = $true; $r.Why = $forgettingWhy; return $r }
9403|        $script:TelemetryLockDepth++
9404|        $r.Ok = $true
9405|        return $r
9406|    }
9407|    try { [void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($p.Home) } catch { $r.Why = "the codex home $($p.Home) could not be made ($(ConvertTo-OneLine $_.Exception.Message))"; return $r }
9408|    $watch = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
9409|    $fs = $null
9410|    while ($null -eq $fs) {
9411|        if (-not $IgnoreMarker -and [IO.File]::Exists($p.Forgetting)) { $r.Forgetting = $true; $r.Why = $forgettingWhy; return $r }
9412|        try { $fs = New-Object System.IO.FileStream($p.TelLock, [System.IO.FileMode]::OpenOrCreate, [System.IO.FileAccess]::ReadWrite, [System.IO.FileShare]::None) } catch {
9413|            if ($watch.ElapsedMilliseconds -ge $WaitMs) { $r.Why = "the telemetry lock $($p.TelLock) stayed busy for $([Math]::Round($WaitMs / 1000.0, 1)) s"; return $r }

168|function Get-PidIdentity {
169|    param([int]$ProcessId, [string]$StartTime = '')
170|    if ($ProcessId -le 0) { return 'gone' }
171|    $live = Get-ProcessStartIso -ProcessId $ProcessId
172|    if ($null -eq $live) { return 'gone' }
173|    if (-not $StartTime -or -not $live) { return 'unknown' }
174|    if (Test-SameStartTime -A $live -B $StartTime) { return 'alive' }
175|    return 'gone'
176|}
177|
178|# A pid counts as alive when a process with that id exists and - if a start time was
179|# recorded for it - still has that start time (otherwise the pid was reused). (wave 28c, D8) An
180|# identity that cannot be confirmed ('unknown' of Get-PidIdentity) counts as ALIVE here: a holder is
181|# never taken over, a survivor never released, on a guess.
182|function Test-PidAlive {
183|    param([int]$ProcessId, [string]$StartTime = '')
184|    if ($ProcessId -le 0) { return $false }
185|    $live = Get-ProcessStartIso -ProcessId $ProcessId
186|    if ($null -eq $live) { return $false }
187|    if ($StartTime -and $live -and -not (Test-SameStartTime -A $live -B $StartTime)) { return $false }
188|    return $true
189|}
190|
191|# (wave 28, R17) The telemetry switch - shared with the SessionStart hook, which prints it. A run's
192|# -Telemetry on|off ($Override) wins; else CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY: unset or empty - ON (the
193|# default); on, 1, true, yes - on; off, 0, false, no, none - off; ANY OTHER VALUE counts as off (a
194|# switch that cannot be read never sends). Reads the environment only. { On; Text ('on' | 'off');
195|# Source ('-Telemetry' | 'the default' | 'CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY' | ... (not on or off: counts as
196|# off)) }.
197|function Get-TelemetrySwitch {
198|    param([string]$Override = '')
199|    $o = ([string]$Override).Trim().ToLowerInvariant()
200|    if ($o -eq 'on' -or $o -eq 'off') { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = ($o -eq 'on'); Text = $o; Source = '-Telemetry' } }
201|    $v = ([string][Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY')).Trim().ToLowerInvariant()
202|    if (-not $v) { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $true; Text = 'on'; Source = 'the default' } }
203|    if (@('on', '1', 'true', 'yes') -contains $v) { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $true; Text = 'on'; Source = 'CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY' } }
204|    if (@('off', '0', 'false', 'no', 'none') -contains $v) { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $false; Text = 'off'; Source = 'CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY' } }
205|    return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $false; Text = 'off'; Source = "CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY='$v' (not on or off: counts as off)" }
206|}
207|
208|# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- detached runs (wave 25, R12): the readers
209|#
210|# codex-consult.ps1 -Detach checks a consultation like a real run in the caller's process (the
211|# dry run's checks plus those a real run makes before it takes the task lock - D2), then runs it
212|# in a BACKGROUND process and returns at once. The run's state is its status file
213|# <task>/.consult.detached-<id8>.status.json (atomic replace; <id8> = the first 8 hex digits of
214|# the detach id, a guid), its console output (stdout and stderr) the log
215|# <task>/.consult.detached-<id8>.log. Both names start with .consult.: Get-CollabSnapshot leaves
216|# them out (an agy or muse member's tree check never sees them), the collab directory is outside
217|# the tree fingerprint, and .gitignore carries .consult.detached-* (D1).
218|# Writers (D5): the foreground writes `starting` (no pid) ONCE, before it launches the
219|# background, never after; from then on only the background writes - its self-report `running`
220|# {pid, start_time, host} first, the members as they start and finish, `done` {exit, summary} on
221|# EVERY exit path (D3); `codex-consult.ps1 -Status -Prune` deletes the files of runs that are done
222|# or died, 7 days after (D6) - (wave 26, F07-1) an unreadable status file too, 7 days after the
223|# file was last written. Readers - -Status, -Wait, codex-findings.ps1 -List, the SessionStart
224|# hook - judge a record that is not done by its background's liveness (Get-DetachedJudgement, D6);
225|# a background on another host is never judged (D11).
226|#
227|# The record (status_version 1), fields in this order: status_version, id (the guid), id8, task,
228|# kind (run | panel), state (starting | running | done), exit (null until done), started (the
229|# foreground's clock), updated, finished, wall_seconds, pid, start_time (the background's: UTC
230|# round trip), host, budget_sec (D4 - -Wait's default timeout), purpose, reply_name, brief,
231|# members[{position (the roster position; 1 without a roster), lineage, state (D11: pending |
232|# running | usable | failed | skipped | killed | blocked | commit_blocked | orphan), outcome (the
233|# panel's Get-PanelMemberStatus phrase; a single run: its bridge outcome), wall_seconds, n,
234|# handoff (NN), reply}], summary (the summary block the run printed - a single run: its outcome
235|# lines up to `events file:`; a panel: its `Panel <id8>: ...` block - else its last error line),
236|# log, args (only in the foreground's `starting` record: the background's parameters, base64 of
237|# UTF-8 PowerShell CLIXML; the self-report drops it).
238|
239|$script:DetachedStatusVersion = 1
240|# D5: a `starting` record without a pid reads "starting" this long, then "never started"
241|$script:DetachedStartGraceSec = 60
242|# D6: -Status -Prune removes the runs that are done or died after this many days
243|$script:DetachedPruneDays = 7
244|# D11: a member's state
245|$script:DetachedMemberStates = @('pending', 'running', 'usable', 'failed', 'skipped', 'killed', 'blocked', 'commit_blocked', 'orphan')
246|# "k of N members finished": the member states that count as finished (a skipped entry never ran)
247|$script:DetachedMemberDone = @('usable', 'failed', 'killed', 'blocked', 'commit_blocked', 'orphan')
248|
249|# The files of a detached run: { Id8; Status; Log; Prompt (wave 26, F11-2: the inline -Prompt of
250|# a run that has not started yet) }.
251|function Get-DetachedPaths {
252|    param([string]$TaskDir, [string]$Id)
253|    $id8 = ([string]$Id).Replace('-', '')
254|    if ($id8.Length -gt 8) { $id8 = $id8.Substring(0, 8) }
255|    $id8 = $id8.ToLowerInvariant()
256|    return [pscustomobject]@{ Id8 = $id8; Status = (Join-Path $TaskDir ".consult.detached-$id8.status.json"); Log = (Join-Path $TaskDir ".consult.detached-$id8.log"); Prompt = (Join-Path $TaskDir ".consult.detached-$id8.prompt.txt") }

168|function Get-PidIdentity {
169|    param([int]$ProcessId, [string]$StartTime = '')
170|    if ($ProcessId -le 0) { return 'gone' }
171|    $live = Get-ProcessStartIso -ProcessId $ProcessId
172|    if ($null -eq $live) { return 'gone' }
173|    if (-not $StartTime -or -not $live) { return 'unknown' }
174|    if (Test-SameStartTime -A $live -B $StartTime) { return 'alive' }
175|    return 'gone'

178|# A pid counts as alive when a process with that id exists and - if a start time was
179|# recorded for it - still has that start time (otherwise the pid was reused). (wave 28c, D8) An
180|# identity that cannot be confirmed ('unknown' of Get-PidIdentity) counts as ALIVE here: a holder is
181|# never taken over, a survivor never released, on a guess.
182|function Test-PidAlive {
183|    param([int]$ProcessId, [string]$StartTime = '')
184|    if ($ProcessId -le 0) { return $false }
185|    $live = Get-ProcessStartIso -ProcessId $ProcessId
186|    if ($null -eq $live) { return $false }
187|    if ($StartTime -and $live -and -not (Test-SameStartTime -A $live -B $StartTime)) { return $false }
188|    return $true
189|}

191|# (wave 28, R17) The telemetry switch - shared with the SessionStart hook, which prints it. A run's
192|# -Telemetry on|off ($Override) wins; else CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY: unset or empty - ON (the
193|# default); on, 1, true, yes - on; off, 0, false, no, none - off; ANY OTHER VALUE counts as off (a
194|# switch that cannot be read never sends). Reads the environment only. { On; Text ('on' | 'off');
195|# Source ('-Telemetry' | 'the default' | 'CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY' | ... (not on or off: counts as
196|# off)) }.
197|function Get-TelemetrySwitch {
198|    param([string]$Override = '')
199|    $o = ([string]$Override).Trim().ToLowerInvariant()
200|    if ($o -eq 'on' -or $o -eq 'off') { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = ($o -eq 'on'); Text = $o; Source = '-Telemetry' } }
201|    $v = ([string][Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY')).Trim().ToLowerInvariant()
202|    if (-not $v) { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $true; Text = 'on'; Source = 'the default' } }
203|    if (@('on', '1', 'true', 'yes') -contains $v) { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $true; Text = 'on'; Source = 'CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY' } }
204|    if (@('off', '0', 'false', 'no', 'none') -contains $v) { return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $false; Text = 'off'; Source = 'CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY' } }
205|    return [pscustomobject]@{ On = $false; Text = 'off'; Source = "CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY='$v' (not on or off: counts as off)" }

208|# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- detached runs (wave 25, R12): the readers
209|#
210|# codex-consult.ps1 -Detach checks a consultation like a real run in the caller's process (the
211|# dry run's checks plus those a real run makes before it takes the task lock - D2), then runs it
212|# in a BACKGROUND process and returns at once. The run's state is its status file
213|# <task>/.consult.detached-<id8>.status.json (atomic replace; <id8> = the first 8 hex digits of
214|# the detach id, a guid), its console output (stdout and stderr) the log
215|# <task>/.consult.detached-<id8>.log. Both names start with .consult.: Get-CollabSnapshot leaves
216|# them out (an agy or muse member's tree check never sees them), the collab directory is outside
217|# the tree fingerprint, and .gitignore carries .consult.detached-* (D1).
218|# Writers (D5): the foreground writes `starting` (no pid) ONCE, before it launches the
219|# background, never after; from then on only the background writes - its self-report `running`
220|# {pid, start_time, host} first, the members as they start and finish, `done` {exit, summary} on
221|# EVERY exit path (D3); `codex-consult.ps1 -Status -Prune` deletes the files of runs that are done
222|# or died, 7 days after (D6) - (wave 26, F07-1) an unreadable status file too, 7 days after the
223|# file was last written. Readers - -Status, -Wait, codex-findings.ps1 -List, the SessionStart
224|# hook - judge a record that is not done by its background's liveness (Get-DetachedJudgement, D6);
225|# a background on another host is never judged (D11).
226|#
227|# The record (status_version 1), fields in this order: status_version, id (the guid), id8, task,
228|# kind (run | panel), state (starting | running | done), exit (null until done), started (the
229|# foreground's clock), updated, finished, wall_seconds, pid, start_time (the background's: UTC
230|# round trip), host, budget_sec (D4 - -Wait's default timeout), purpose, reply_name, brief,
231|# members[{position (the roster position; 1 without a roster), lineage, state (D11: pending |
232|# running | usable | failed | skipped | killed | blocked | commit_blocked | orphan), outcome (the
233|# panel's Get-PanelMemberStatus phrase; a single run: its bridge outcome), wall_seconds, n,
234|# handoff (NN), reply}], summary (the summary block the run printed - a single run: its outcome
235|# lines up to `events file:`; a panel: its `Panel <id8>: ...` block - else its last error line),
236|# log, args (only in the foreground's `starting` record: the background's parameters, base64 of
237|# UTF-8 PowerShell CLIXML; the self-report drops it).
238|
239|$script:DetachedStatusVersion = 1
240|# D5: a `starting` record without a pid reads "starting" this long, then "never started"
241|$script:DetachedStartGraceSec = 60
242|# D6: -Status -Prune removes the runs that are done or died after this many days
243|$script:DetachedPruneDays = 7
244|# D11: a member's state
245|$script:DetachedMemberStates = @('pending', 'running', 'usable', 'failed', 'skipped', 'killed', 'blocked', 'commit_blocked', 'orphan')
246|# "k of N members finished": the member states that count as finished (a skipped entry never ran)
247|$script:DetachedMemberDone = @('usable', 'failed', 'killed', 'blocked', 'commit_blocked', 'orphan')
248|
249|# The files of a detached run: { Id8; Status; Log; Prompt (wave 26, F11-2: the inline -Prompt of
250|# a run that has not started yet) }.
251|function Get-DetachedPaths {
252|    param([string]$TaskDir, [string]$Id)
253|    $id8 = ([string]$Id).Replace('-', '')
254|    if ($id8.Length -gt 8) { $id8 = $id8.Substring(0, 8) }
255|    $id8 = $id8.ToLowerInvariant()
256|    return [pscustomobject]@{ Id8 = $id8; Status = (Join-Path $TaskDir ".consult.detached-$id8.status.json"); Log = (Join-Path $TaskDir ".consult.detached-$id8.log"); Prompt = (Join-Path $TaskDir ".consult.detached-$id8.prompt.txt") }

README.md:3058:| `CODEX_CONSULT_NOW`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_SURVIVORS`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_DETACH_GUIDS`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_PANEL_SEED`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_TELEMETRY_ENV`, (wave 28b) `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_REGISTER_FAIL`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_HEALTH_FAIL_FIRST`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_TELEMETRY_REQUEST_MS`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_MS`, (wave 28c) `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_START_UNREADABLE` | tests only | test hooks; never set them in normal use - (wave 27c, D14) they are honoured ONLY while `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1` is set too (every harness and `run-all.ps1` set it); without it they are ignored and a run warns once: `test hook(s) ignored - CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1 is not set: <names>` (`CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_PANEL_SEED`: the routing seed's nonce when `-PanelSeed` is not given; (wave 28; wave 28b) `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_TELEMETRY_ENV=<path>`: the telemetry sender writes there the NAMES of every variable of its environment; (wave 28b) `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_REGISTER_FAIL=1`: the registration write of the engine process fails (D19); `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_HEALTH_FAIL_FIRST=1`: the first endpoint update of a run fails (D13); `..._TELEMETRY_REQUEST_MS` / `..._FLUSH_MS`: the sender's bounds). (wave 28b, D10) A run that finds `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1` says `test mode is ON: test hooks are honoured` on the console and in `warnings[]`; no ENGINE child (a turn, a launcher probe) gets `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE` or any `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_*` variable - a panel member and the detached background (the bridge itself) keep them, the telemetry sender gets only the test mode and its own hooks. (wave 28c, D12) Where the line appears: the console of a committed run (after the commit) and its `warnings[]`, a dry run (with the other run warnings, and its preview's `warnings[]`), a -Panel run (the panel's lines, and each member's `warnings[]`), a detached run (its foreground's lines and the background's entry) - NOT on a refused run: a refusal stops before anything starts or is written. (wave 28c) `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_START_UNREADABLE=<pid>[,<pid>]`: these pids read as a process whose start time cannot be read (D8); `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_KILL_DENIED=taskkill`: only `taskkill` is denied (`=1` denies the enumeration too) |
